title: async def (Event Loop) vs def (anyio Worker Thread Pool Execution)

progressiveExplaining.eli5: If you write `async def`, you are promising: 'I will never freeze or sleep; I will only use non-blocking tools'. If you break this promise and run a slow blocking task inside `async def`, you freeze the entire server for everyone. If you write plain `def`, FastAPI knows you might be slow and sends your function to an external helper thread so the main event loop never stutters.
progressiveExplaining.junior: In FastAPI, route handlers can be defined with `async def` or plain `def`. Use `async def` when calling asynchronous libraries using `await` (e.g. `httpx`, `asyncpg`). Use plain `def` for standard synchronous blocking code (e.g. `time.sleep()`, standard `requests`, synchronous database drivers like standard `psycopg2` or `sqlite3`). FastAPI automatically runs plain `def` endpoints in a separate background thread pool (`anyio.to_thread.run_sync`).
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, this dual-mode execution prevents event loop starvation. An `async def` handler executes directly on the single-threaded asyncio event loop. Calling synchronous blocking I/O (e.g. `requests.get()`) inside `async def` blocks the event loop, preventing all concurrent requests from making progress. Plain `def` functions are offloaded to `anyio`'s thread pool worker threads (default max 40 threads), allowing synchronous blocking calls to execute without blocking the main event loop.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: FastAPI checks `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(endpoint)`. If `True`, it awaits the coroutine directly: `await endpoint(**solved_params)`. If `False`, it dispatches the function via `anyio.to_thread.run_sync(endpoint_with_params)`. The worker thread acquires the GIL, executes the synchronous function, and posts the result back to the event loop's task queue upon completion.

codeComparison.title: Event Loop Blocking Bug vs Safe anyio Thread Pool Execution
codeComparison.summary: Synchronous blocking code inside `async def` freezes the entire server; using plain `def` offloads to worker threads safely.

legacyOrBad.label: Blocking Call inside async def (Critical Bug)
legacyOrBad.snippet: async def endpoint(): time.sleep(5) # ❌ Freezes the entire server for all users!

fullFile.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
import time

app = FastAPI()

# ❌ CRITICAL BUG: time.sleep() blocks the single-threaded event loop!
# While this request runs for 5 seconds, NO OTHER REQUEST can be processed.
@app.get('/blocking-async')
async def blocking_endpoint():
  time.sleep(5) # ❌ Freezes event loop
  return {'status': 'done'}

modernOrGood.label: Plain def Threadpool Offload
modernOrGood.snippet: def safe_endpoint(): time.sleep(5) # ✅ NEW: Offloaded to worker threadpool automatically

interviewGotchas.question: What happens under load if you use standard synchronous `def` for all endpoints in FastAPI?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of thread pool saturation in FastAPI.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: While plain `def` avoids blocking the event loop, it offloads to the `anyio` worker thread pool, which has a default limit of **40 worker threads**. If 100 concurrent requests hit slow synchronous `def` endpoints (each taking 1 second), 40 requests will occupy the threads, and the remaining 60 requests will queue up in the thread pool backlog, increasing latency. For high-concurrency I/O, true non-blocking `async def` with async drivers scales to thousands of concurrent requests.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not assume plain `def` scales infinitely; it is bounded by the worker thread pool capacity.

interviewGotchas.question: If you must call a blocking synchronous library from inside an `async def` endpoint, how should you do it?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of manual thread offloading in async code.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer:
Use `anyio.to_thread.run_sync()` or `asyncio.to_thread()` (Python 3.9+):
```python
import asyncio
@app.get('/process')
async def process():
  result = await asyncio.to_thread(legacy_blocking_function, arg1)
  return result
```
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Never call a blocking synchronous function directly inside `async def` without `asyncio.to_thread()`.
